questions.question: Prime cost is:
options: Direct materials plus direct labour — the spending that touches the product directly

questions.question: The wages of a floor supervisor overseeing five production teams are classified as:
options: Indirect labour, included in factory overheads

questions.question: Rent of the showroom where finished shoes are displayed for sale is:
options: A selling and distribution cost — the word FACTORY in factory overheads matters

questions.question: The three stocks of a manufacturer are:
options: Raw materials, work-in-progress and finished goods

questions.question: Opening raw materials R60 000, purchases R560 000, carriage R25 000, closing raw materials R95 000. Direct material cost is:
options: R550 000 — materials available less what still lies unused in the storeroom

questions.question: Prime cost of R900 000 plus factory overheads of R390 000 gives:
options: Cost of production of finished goods

questions.question: Opening work-in-progress was R40 000 and closing work-in-progress R80 000. The adjustment to total manufacturing cost of R1 290 000 gives cost of production of finished goods of:
options: R1 250 000 — add the opening, subtract the closing

questions.question: Cost of production of R1 250 000 for 50 000 finished pairs gives a unit cost of:

subtopics.title: From Factory Floor to Income Statement

questions.question: Opening finished goods R100 000 plus cost of production R1 250 000 less closing finished goods R150 000 gives cost of sales of:
Sales of R1 680 000 against cost of sales of R1 200 000 confirms a mark-up on cost of:
options: 40 percent — gross profit of R480 000 over cost of sales

questions.question: Depreciation on delivery vehicles belongs in:
options: Selling and distribution cost — classified by what the spending served

questions.question: When one building houses both the factory and the office, rent is split by:

subtopics.title: Break-Even and the Ethics of Making Things

questions.question: Selling price R35, variable cost R23 per unit, fixed costs R540 000. The break-even point is:
options: 45 000 units — fixed costs divided by the contribution of R12

questions.question: Producing and selling 48 000 units against a break-even of 45 000 means:
options: The business runs at a loss
A cushion of 3 000 units, each contributing R12 of pure profit
Fixed costs are not fully covered

questions.question: If raw materials become more expensive while the selling price stays fixed, the break-even point:
options: Climbs — the contribution per unit narrows, so more units are needed to cover fixed costs

questions.question: Competitors agreeing with each other on selling prices is:
options: Price fixing — illegal collusion against the consumer

questions.question: At Ma Zondi's stand, the flour, yeast, oil and mince are:
options: Direct materials — they become the product

questions.question: The gas bottle and the monthly stall fee are overheads because:
options: Nobody can say which vetkoek used which rand of them — real costs, spread across everything

questions.question: At nine o'clock, the shaped dough waiting its turn in the oil is:
The counter book Ma Zondi records orders in belongs to:
options: The business-running costs — office, not the stand's making costs

questions.question: Ma Zondi bought R8 500 of ingredients but R1 200 remains in the pantry. The month's materials cost is:
options: R7 300 — the pantry costs nothing to this month's vetkoek

questions.question: Stand total R14 700, opening dough tray R300, closing dough tray R600. Finished production cost is:
options: R14 400 — add the opening tray, leave out the closing one

questions.question: R14 400 of finished production across 1 200 vetkoek gives a unit cost of:
options: R12 — and selling at R18 leaves R6 of gross margin each

questions.question: The granddaughter's question really taught that:
options: Vetkoek should cost less to make
Unit costs only matter to big factories
Money spent this month and production finished this month are different things — the pantry and the dough tray hold the difference

subtopics.title: How Many Must She Sell Before She Smiles?

questions.question: A stall fee of R4 800 a month and a contribution of R8 per vetkoek give a break-even of:
options: 600 vetkoek — number 601 is the first that feeds the family

questions.question: The proof that 600 is break-even is:
options: 600 times R8 equals R4 800 of profit
R10 800 in from sales, R6 000 of ingredients and R4 800 of stall fee out — exactly zero
The stall fee equals the sales

questions.question: If mince prices push the variable cost to R12 per vetkoek, break-even:
options: Jumps to 800 — the contribution narrows to R6

questions.question: Opening a second stand with R4 800 more in fixed fees illustrates that:
options: Fixed costs fall as businesses grow
Growth raises the pile to cover before the first extra unit sells — the break-even doubles to 1 200
